issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (Europe)

plan.diagnosis: Horizon Pacific Metals KG (Germany) represents USD 1,223,450 in annual spend with a concerning resiliency score of 48/100 and reliance on 56 sub-tier suppliers, creating single-source dependency risk at the subtier level in Europe. Despite zero disruption events in the past 12 months, the low resiliency score indicates structural vulnerability in the supply chain that could impact USD 1.22M in expenditure.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct immediate sub-tier mapping exercise with Horizon Pacific Metals KG to identify the critical single-source subtier supplier(s) among the 56 and document dependencies, lead times, and risk exposure
Issue RFI to 3-5 alternative Europe-based metals suppliers to assess capability to replicate Horizon Pacific's scope and validate sub-tier diversification in their supply base
Negotiate contractual right-to-audit clause and require Horizon Pacific to qualify at least one backup subtier supplier for critical materials, with quarterly sub-tier risk reporting
Qualify and onboard one alternate supplier across all ERPs (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa) with target 70/30 spend split to reduce single-source exposure
Implement dual-source purchasing policy with 30% of USD 1,223,450 spend (USD 367,035) redirected to alternate supplier by end of remediation period

plan.expected_impact: Mitigate single-source subtier risk exposure on USD 1,223,450 annual spend and improve supply chain resiliency score from 48 to target 70+ through dual sourcing strategy.
kpis: Sub-tier supplier diversification: reduce single-source subtier dependencies from 100% to <30% within 6 months
Spend diversification: achieve 70/30 split (USD 856,415 / USD 367,035) between primary and alternate supplier by week 16
Resiliency score improvement: increase from 48 to 70+ within 6 months
Sub-tier visibility: 100% mapping of critical sub-tier suppliers (target top 10 of 56) by week 2
Alternate supplier qualification rate: onboard minimum 1 qualified alternate by week 12
risks: Price increase risk: alternate suppliers may quote 5-15% premium over current USD 1,223,450 spend base, adding USD 61,173-183,518 annually
Qualification timeline risk: 12-week alternate supplier onboarding may extend if technical approvals or quality validations fail
Incumbent resistance: Horizon Pacific may resist sub-tier transparency requirements or contractual audits, delaying mapping exercise
ERP integration complexity: onboarding alternate across 5 ERP systems (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa) creates data consistency and payment term configuration risks
Volume commitment: splitting USD 1,223,450 spend may trigger minimum order quantity issues or loss of volume discounts with Horizon Pacific
erp_actions: SAP: create vendor master for qualified alternate supplier in LFA1/LFB1 with same company codes as Horizon Pacific; establish source list (ME01) with 70/30 quota arrangement for relevant materials
SAP: add sub-tier risk monitoring flag in vendor master (LFA1) custom field for Horizon Pacific and set review interval to quarterly
Oracle EBS: create supplier record for alternate in AP module and mirror site assignments to Horizon Pacific; configure dual-source ASL (Approved Supplier List) entries with allocation percentages
Dynamics 365 & NetSuite: onboard alternate supplier with matching procurement categories and establish requisition rules to enforce 70/30 allocation across purchase orders
Coupa: update supplier records with sub-tier risk scores; configure sourcing events to include sub-tier diversification criteria (minimum 2 subtier sources) in future RFx for metals category
All ERPs: implement PO approval workflow flag for any single supplier exceeding 80% of metals category spend (USD 978,760 threshold) to enforce dual-source policy
